title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, and ADR Process
author: Maya Carter
summary: Consolidated company-wide architecture and engineering standards covering API design, coding practices, infrastructure and IaC, model-serving requirements, observability expectations, performance SLOs, and the decision record (ADR) process.
body:
Purpose

This document defines Redwood Inference's canonical architecture and engineering standards. Its goal is to ensure consistent, secure, and observable services and model-serving endpoints across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. These standards are normative: teams are expected to follow them or produce an ADR describing trade-offs and mitigation plans.

Scope

Applies to all service and model-serving work in the Redwood codebase and platform: public APIs, internal microservices, runtime components (inference runtime, router, cache), provisioning IaC, and customer-facing deployment artifacts. Does not replace team-level conventions but provides company-level constraints and minimal acceptable controls.

Ownership and Review

- Owned by: Architecture & Platform guild (eng-platform)
- Primary contact: eng-standards@redwood.ai
- Review cadence: annual or on major platform changes (new runtime, major infra provider changes)
- Reviewers for this version: Diego Alvarez, Priya Nair

1) API Standards

Overview
- All external and internal HTTP APIs must be defined with OpenAPI v3.1 and stored in the central API registry (git:infra/api-definitions).
- Machine-readable schemas (JSON Schema) are required for request and response bodies to enable validation, contract tests, and SDK generation.

Versioning and Compatibility
- Use Semantic Versioning for public-facing APIs: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.
- Breaking changes require a documented migration plan and a deprecation period of at least 90 days for hosted endpoints; Dedicated/Private customers must be notified 120 days in advance.
- Support multiple API versions concurrently for at least one MAJOR version transition window.

Design Principles
- Favor explicit error codes and typed error bodies: {"code": "INVALID_PROMPT", "message": "...", "status": 400}.
- Use consistent pagination and filtering patterns across services. Prefer cursor-based pagination for large result sets.
- Authentication: OAuth2 bearer tokens for user scopes; mTLS for service-to-service and private deployments.
- Rate limiting: 429 responses must include X-RateLimit-Reset header and a Retry-After when appropriate.

API Example (OpenAPI excerpt)
```yaml
openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Redwood Generation API
  version: 1.0.0
paths:
  /v1/generate:
    post:
      summary: Generate text for a prompt
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: '#/components/schemas/GenerateRequest'
      responses:
        '200':
          description: successful response
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/GenerateResponse'
components:
  schemas:
    GenerateRequest:
      type: object
      properties:
        model:
          type: string
        prompt:
          type: string
    GenerateResponse:
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
        output:
          type: string
```

2) Coding Standards

General rules
- Language-level style: adopt the dominant style for the repository (Go: gofmt + golangci-lint; Python: black + ruff; TypeScript: prettier + eslint).
- All production code must include unit tests with >= 80% coverage for critical path code (model routers, auth, billing).
- PRs: require two approvers from distinct teams for cross-service changes; a single approver may be sufficient for small, isolated changes.

Repository layout and naming
- Services use the pattern: service-<domain> (e.g., service-router, service-embedder).
- Protobuf and API contracts live in infra/api-definitions and are the single source of truth. Generated code should be committed to a build-artifacts ignore list and rebuilt during CI.

Secrets and keys
- No plaintext secrets in repo. Use the secrets manager and reference secrets via environment variables populated by deployment configs. Scanning tools (git-secrets) run in CI.

3) Infrastructure & IaC Standards

Principles
- All cloud resources must be provisioned through Terraform (infra/terraform) with modules for common patterns. Ad-hoc resources are disallowed.
- Environments: dev, staging, prod. Namespaced resource naming: redwood-<env>-<service>-<resource>.

Networking and security
- Private subnets for runtime VMs; NAT/egress restricted via controlled egress gateways for prod.
- Default ingress: deny. Use the platform ingress controller (K8s ALB or cloud load balancer) with WAF rules for public endpoints.
- IAM: least privilege for all roles and service principals. Long-lived keys are prohibited for new services.

Terraform workflow
1. Create feature branch against infra repo.
2. Open PR with tfplan attached from CI.
3. Two approvers required for prod changes; one approver for dev/staging.
4. Apply via automated run pipeline (no direct manual applies).

4) Model-Serving Standards

Model artifacts and packaging
- Models are versioned and stored in the model registry with an immutable artifact ID: <model-name>@sha256:<hash>.
- Packaging includes a manifest (YAML) listing architecture, tokenizer, expected kv-cache shape, max sequence length, and quantization profile. Example fields: architecture=transformer-xl, max_seq_len=8192, kv_dtype=float16.

Serving guarantees
- Every served model must include a performance profile (throughput tokens/s, cold-start time, peak memory) generated by standardized bench harness (eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite).
- Default runtime behavior: continuous batching enabled, prefix KV cache for identical request prefixes, and token-level streaming support where applicable.

Safety and testing
- Model QA: each model onboarding must include an eval suite (prompt sets) with acceptance thresholds for safety and utility. Models failing thresholds cannot be promoted to hosted catalog.
- Canary rollout for model updates: 0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated quality checks at each stage.

5) Observability Standards

Metrics (all services)
- Required metrics: request.count, request.error_count, request.latency_ms (histogram with buckets), tokens.generated, cache.hit_rate, batch.size.
- Labels/tags: service, env, model (if applicable), route, region, deployment_version.

Tracing and logs
- Trace sampling: default 10% with 100% sample for requests with errors or latencies > p95 SLO. Use W3C trace context for cross-service propagation.
- Structured JSON request/response logs at INFO. Do not log plaintext PII or customer prompts in production; prompts may be redacted or stored in an encrypted audit store if required by feature and with approval.

Dashboards and alerts
- Standard dashboards: per-service overview, per-model latency/cost, token consumption, error budget burn. Templates: dashboards/service-overview and dashboards/model-latency.
- Alerts: page when SLO error budget burn exceeds 5% within a 1-hour window or absolute error rate > 1% for 5 minutes. Pager duty runbooks must be linked in the alert.

6) Performance Standards and SLOs

SLOs (example baseline)
- Availability: 99.95% for Hosted control plane APIs; 99.9% for model serving endpoints (depending on tier).
- Latency: p95 <= 250ms for short-chat requests (< 256 tokens) on Hosted default model; p95 <= 600ms for generation requests up to 1024 tokens. Dedicated customers may set custom SLOs in contracts.
- Error rate: < 0.5% for production traffic, with automated rollback if sustained > 1% for 10 minutes.

Performance guidance
- Use prefix caching and batching to reduce per-token cost for high-throughput workloads. Default batch size cap set to 64 unless otherwise tuned by perf profile.
- Quantization: recommend int8 or llm-int8 for CPU-based Dedicated deployments; document model-specific quantization profiles in quantization-profiles/ with performance delta expectations.

7) ADR (Architecture Decision Record) Process

When to open an ADR
- Any change to cross-cutting platform behavior (auth, API contract, routing, runtime kernel choices), long-lived exceptions to standards, or significant infra cost/architecture changes.

ADR format (required fields)
- Title
- Status: proposed | accepted | superseded | deprecated
- Context
- Decision (what we chose)
- Consequences
- Rollout and migration plan

ADR workflow
1. Draft ADR in the architecture-and-standards git repo under adrs/.
2. Link the ADR in the related Confluence page and open a PR.
3. Discussion period: 5 business days for urgent items, 10 business days for major changes.
4. Approval: architecture guild sign-off required for changes to platform defaults; product/security sign-off required if user-facing or compliance-relevant.

Example ADRs (links)
- ADR-001: Standardizing API error model -> /confluence/architecture-and-standards/architecture-standards-api-coding-infra-model-observability-adr-2026-02-20
- ADR-014: Choice of continuous batching runtime kernel -> /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/adr-014

8) Rollout and Release Checklist

Before promoting to production:
1. API contract validated against consumer tests.
2. Performance benchmark completed and meets perf-profile targets.
3. Security review (SAST + dependency scan) completed.
4. Observability: dashboards created and alerting configured.
5. Runbook and rollback steps documented and linked.
6. ADR raised/updated if the change introduces a platform-level change.

9) Exceptions and Governance

- Temporary exceptions: allowed for up to 30 days with documented mitigation and an assigned owner. Longer exceptions require a formal ADR and architecture guild approval.
- Periodic audits: eng-platform will run bi-annual audits for compliance with IaC, secrets, and observability standards.

References and Templates
- API contract template: infra/api-definitions/templates/openapi-template.yaml
- ADR template: infra/architecture/adrs/adr-template.md
- Bench harness: eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/README.md
- Terraform module catalog: infra/terraform/modules/README.md

Appendix: Common Error Codes
- INVALID_REQUEST: 400 - client request is malformed
- UNAUTHORIZED: 401 - auth failure
- RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED: 429
- MODEL_NOT_AVAILABLE: 503 - model region/capacity unavailable
- INTERNAL_ERROR: 500 - server side error
